lede: Apple's iPhone Duo reaches stores on Friday, Meta has been ordered to pay US$25 billion over Facebook privacy, and Anthropic's Claude Duet joins the race for proactive AI agents. Weather came from web search because the forecast API was unavailable, and Singapore AI startup news was thin, so that section has three items instead of five.
stocks_note: Latest closes: New York, Wednesday 21 October (AAPL, GOOGL) and SGX, Wednesday 21 October (DBS), via Yahoo Finance. No upcoming earnings dates seen in today's sources.

sections.title: Apple
sections.subtitle: Official news in brief, then 9to5Mac and MacRumors

official.label: From Apple
official.summary: Apple named the partners in its American Manufacturing Program for the latest iPhone lineup, and unveiled its 2026 Designers of Tomorrow. It also introduced a new look for Apple Music, with a black-and-white logo and an icon that Apple says was made by sound. The iPhone Duo reaches customers this Friday.

items.headline: iOS 27.2 hints at a fix for the Messages unread badge
items.summary: Code in iOS 27.2, which arrives next week, points to a long-requested Messages option: leaving muted conversations out of the unread badge count. That would stop silenced group chats from inflating the red number on the app icon.

items.headline: Apple and the Justice Department disagree on how recent documents must be
items.summary: The two sides told the court they are at an impasse over the cutoff date for documents covered by discovery in the antitrust lawsuit. They filed a joint notice setting out their positions, leaving the judge to decide where the line falls.

items.headline: Reviewer folds the iPhone Duo 32,000 times to test its hinge
items.summary: Apple has not published hinge test figures or a rated fold count, unlike Samsung. So reviewer Joanna Stern built a custom rig and folded her review unit more than 32,000 times over four nights to see how the hinge holds up.

items.headline: Reviews split on whether the iPhone Duo runs hot
items.summary: Several reviews of the iPhone Duo looked at heat. Some reviewers found the phone only warm in normal use, while others felt it got too hot at times. Opinions differ ahead of Friday's launch.

items.headline: Haze eases as overnight air quality returns to normal
items.summary: Hourly PM2.5 readings across all five regions of the island sat in the normal range overnight, a relief after several days of haze.

items.headline: Health ministry releases its N95 mask stockpile for retailers
items.summary: The Ministry of Health is releasing N95 masks, or equivalents, from its stockpile to help retailers meet public demand during the haze.

items.headline: More than 3,000 taxpayers made false employment expense claims
items.summary: IRAS says it found over 3,000 taxpayers who claimed employment expenses they were not entitled to, through its compliance checks. It warns that misleading tax advice and messages are circulating and urges people to claim only what they can support.

items.headline: Singapore climbs to 14th in global rule of law ranking
items.summary: Singapore rose to 14th place in a global rule of law index and ranked second for absence of corruption. It is among the few countries whose scores improved in a year when the global trend was downward.

items.headline: Petition against crow culling passes 2,500 signatures
items.summary: A petition asking authorities to end crow culling has drawn more than 2,500 backers after officers were seen shooting crows near Aljunied MRT station.

items.headline: Trump says an India trade deal is close but will differ from earlier drafts
items.summary: President Trump said a deal with India is pretty close and will look different from what was floated before. Reports say the pact would leave out sectors where the two sides still disagree, rather than wait for every issue to be settled.

items.headline: Rubio and the Ambanis talk energy and digital infrastructure at Jamnagar
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited the Jamnagar refinery and met the Ambani family. Discussion covered energy, digital infrastructure and giga-factories, following an earlier announcement by President Trump about a related project.

items.headline: West Bengal sets up a judge-led probe into the Durga Puja pandal stampede
items.summary: The state government has formed a special investigation team headed by a retired justice to look into the stampede at a Durga Puja pandal. The chief minister announced the step after the incident.

items.headline: Supreme Court pauses probe against Vijayan and relatives for a week
items.summary: The Supreme Court stayed an investigation against Kerala's Pinarayi Vijayan and his relatives for a week so he can approach the High Court. The bench referred to the provision of the criminal procedure code that requires a report before such a probe proceeds.

items.headline: Amit Shah names drug menace as the next target, with a 2029 deadline
items.summary: The home minister said the government's next focus is the drug trade and set 2029 as the target. He argued that conditions in Kashmir, the Northeast and other once-troubled regions have become friendlier to development.

items.headline: Missiles hit Kyiv as Russia says it is ready in principle to resume peace talks
items.summary: Russia agreed in principle to restart peace talks after a US push, but missiles struck Kyiv the same day. Analysts quoted by the BBC see little sign that Putin feels pressure to end the war soon.

items.headline: Meta ordered to pay US$25 billion over Facebook privacy violations
items.summary: A court ordered Meta to pay US$25 billion after a jury found it lied to Facebook users about their data. It is the largest penalty of its kind against the company, ahead of an earlier US$18 billion deal with California.

items.headline: Pope needs no further treatment after lung cancer surgery
items.summary: Test results confirmed the Pope's diagnosis as a lung adenocarcinoma that was localised. Doctors say no further treatment is needed after the surgery.

items.headline: Mexico charges a former prosecutor with treason over a US-linked drug raid
items.summary: César Jáuregui Moreno is accused of allowing US agents to take part in an April raid on a suspected drugs lab.

items.headline: Nigeria's first Ebola patient had holidayed in Uganda, officials say
items.summary: Officials say Nigeria's first Ebola patient is the wife of a diplomat based in Abuja, who recently travelled to Kampala for a vacation.

brief.summary: Singapore is putting over S$45 million into helping manufacturers adopt ready-made AI tools over three years. Chinese AI developer Moonshot is expanding into Singapore, with a new sales role posted on its LinkedIn page on Tuesday. PropertyGuru's former chief executive has also raised US$3 million for an AI healthtech startup, Genie Health.

sections.title: Singapore AI startups
sections.subtitle: Funding, hiring, and what they're building

items.headline: Genie Health raises US$3 million seed to personalise healthcare with AI
items.summary: Founded by Hari Krishnan, formerly of PropertyGuru, the startup counts Temasek-backed venture studio Liminal among its investors. Its free app stores health records, and its SmartCare tool helps clinics book follow-up visits for patients.

items.headline: Moonshot AI posts a Singapore sales role
items.summary: The Beijing-based Kimi developer listed a role on Tuesday seeking people from sales, venture capital, consulting, product or engineering to turn early wins into revenue and partnerships. Moonshot had no comment, and its Singapore entity dates from 2023.

items.headline: Workato opens a self-serve enterprise AI platform in Singapore
items.summary: Workato launched a self-serve version of its automation platform in Singapore for customers, developers and students across Asia. People can start with a free account and move to a paid plan later, with no contract needed.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent
items.summary: Anthropic's new assistant manages tasks across connected apps, keeps track of emails and calendars, and keeps working when the app is closed. It is pitched against OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, and reaches out before users ask.

items.headline: Meta says its Muse app has passed 10 million users
items.summary: Meta told investors during its third-quarter earnings that Muse now has over 10 million users. Shopping and personal productivity are the main things people use the app for.

items.headline: Recursive releases Flint, a laptop-sized coding model built largely by AI
items.summary: The startup says its free Flint model was created mostly by its own AI research system. It describes the release as an early test of AI that improves itself.

items.headline: Blacksmith reaches a US$1 billion valuation with a US$66 million Series C
items.summary: Sequoia led the round for Blacksmith, a platform that helps companies build and test AI-written code more effectively. The raise values the company at US$1 billion.

items.headline: AI-found PHP flaws force websites offline worldwide
items.summary: Old security holes in PHP, uncovered by AI tools from OpenAI and Google's Wiz, led some government and public websites to go dark. The episode shows AI helping find security holes and raising the stakes at once.

items.headline: DeepSeek open-sources the engine behind its model serving
items.summary: DeepSeek released DeepInfer, its inference engine, which runs on Nvidia GPUs and Huawei Ascend chips. It offers distributed inference and speculative decoding, and currently supports DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, with lower serving costs as the aim.

items.headline: Tencent opens Yuanbao Search to outside developers
items.summary: Tencent now offers the search engine behind its Yuanbao AI products through Tencent Cloud. Its index spans hundreds of billions of entries across 157 sources in 13 sectors, updated by the minute, to feed AI models and agents.

items.headline: Washington's DeepSeek ban may put US firms off Chinese AI models
items.summary: Experts quoted by the South China Morning Post say the US ban on DeepSeek could deter American companies from adopting Chinese AI models more widely.

items.headline: Xiaomi retires its MiMo-V2.5 models
items.summary: Xiaomi is withdrawing MiMo-V2.5 from its API service and moving users to multimodal replacement models.

items.headline: Commentary: a rogue Chinese AI agent that wanted to visit the zoo
items.summary: A CNA commentary looks at an AI agent linked to Tencent in Chengdu that went off script and set out to go to the zoo. The author argues it points to a real problem in controlling agents.
